what_it_shows: Thomann all-categories: 22 top categories incl. Gitarren und Baesse (34,013 items; E-Gitarren, Konzertgitarren, Westerngitarren, E-Baesse, Ukulelen, Bluegrass, Verstaerker, Effekte, Pickups), Drums und Percussion, Tasteninstrumente, Studio, PA, Blasinstrumente (by instrument), Traditionelle Instrumente (Streich, historische Saiten, Meditation, Orchesterschlagwerk, Akkordeons); amps and effects sit under the instrument family

Reverb category list: Electric, Acoustic, Bass Guitars separate; Folk Instruments (accordions, banjos, mandolins, ouds, sitars, ukuleles); Band and Orchestra; Keyboards and Synths (analog/digital/modular/eurorack/drum machines/samplers/pianos/organs); Drums and Percussion; Effects and Pedals by effect type; Amps (combo/head/cab/boutique); Pro Audio; Parts; Accessories; Home Audio separate

Sweetwater menu order: Guitars, Basses, Amps & Effects Pedals, Studio & Recording, Software & Plugins, Microphones & Wireless, Live Sound & Lighting, Keyboards & Synth, DJ & Beat Production, Headphones, Drums & Percussion, Band & Orchestra; Synthesizers split keyboard/module/desktop/rackmount/Eurorack/keytar/theremin; Pianos split upright/grand/digital/stage

Digimart index (615,796 items, 550 shops): about 28 top categories from electric guitar, bass, acoustic, ukulele, classical, drums/percussion, winds, strings, piano, keyboard/synth to DAW, mics, mixers/speakers, effects, amps, accessories, pickups/parts, cables, tuners/metronomes, cases/racks, studio fittings, DJ, headphones, audio, toy instruments and goods, scores, other instruments (wagakki/ethnic, accordion, mallet percussion, harmonica); electric guitars by named design (ST, TL, Les Paul, SG, V, Explorer...), basses PB/JB type, saxophones alto/tenor/soprano; price band and shop area facets; new/used/vintage

MIMO 2011 revision of Hornbostel-Sachs: classes 1 idiophones, 2 membranophones, 3 chordophones, 4 aerophones, 5 electrophones (51 electro-acoustic incl. electric guitar 513 and electric piano 511; 52 electromechanical e.g. Hammond; 53 electronic analogue modules; 54 digital incl. samplers 544); microphones, pickups and loudspeakers are transducers 515; instruments sent to an amplifier and loudspeaker are electrophones

EU CN2026 / HS Chapter 92: 9201 pianos (upright, grand, other), 9202 other string (bowed/other), 9205 wind (brass/other; includes accordions, harmoniums, mouth organs), 9206 percussion, 9207 electrically produced or amplified (keyboard/other), 9208 music boxes and misc, 9209 parts and accessories (strings, metronomes); none of the seven headings names microphones, amplifiers or loudspeakers

Classification systems: Western orchestral families (strings, woodwinds, brass, percussion, keyboards), Hornbostel-Sachs, Indian Natyashastra four-fold (tata, avanaddha, sushira, ghana), Chinese bayin eight materials, Mahillon, Schaeffner, functional classes; notes that catalogues may record several attributes (piano is keyboard, string and chordophone)

Fender tier ladder, eleven tiers: Squier Sonic, Affinity, Classic Vibe, Paranormal; Fender Standard, Player II, Player Plus, Vintera III, American Professional II, American Ultra II, American Vintage II, Custom Shop; says the ladder answers how much guitar, not what it sounds like

Forum thread comparing Gibson/Epiphone and Fender/Squier: Squier and MIM Fender sit in same space as Epiphone, Gibson brands non-US guitars Epiphone while Fender badge is made in Mexico, Japan and US; buyers rank by maker line and country of build, with disagreement

Ishibashi Gakki electric guitar subcategories are named forms by body type: Stratocaster type, Les Paul type, Telecaster type, SG, Flying V, Firebird, Explorer, Jaguar, Jazzmaster, Mustang, Soloist/Dinky, headless, semi-acoustic, full-acoustic, odd-shaped, mini/built-in amp, 7-string and over, left-handed

Baidu Baike eight-sound (bayin) classification by material: metal (bells), stone (chimes), silk (strings), bamboo (flutes), gourd (sheng), clay (xun), leather (drums), wood (zhu, yu); in use from the Zhou dynasty to early Qing

Band instruments sold in three tiers student / step-up (intermediate) / professional with materials, craftsmanship and price ranges (student $400-2,200; step-up $1,500-3,000; pro $3,000+); examples by instrument: Bach TR200 step-up trumpet, Yamaha YAS-480, Buffet E11 vs R13; tiers set per maker line

Violin collections structured by level: Beginning ($299-499), Intermediate ($500-2,000), Advanced ($2,000-5,000), Fine and Timeless professional ($5,000+); professional violins are individual-maker work, student violins factory work
Synthesizers divided by synthesis method (subtractive, additive, FM, wavetable, sample-based, vector, granular, physical modelling); history by analog/digital era; clones as a separate phenomenon
Reverb Band and Orchestra splits Woodwind (saxophones, flutes, clarinets), Brass (trumpets, trombones, tubas), String (violins, upright bass, cellos)

Muztorg (Russia's largest instrument retailer) top level: Guitars, Ukulele, Keyboard instruments, Percussion, Microphones and radio systems, DJ, Studio, Sound, Light, Headphones, Cabling, Wind instruments, Harmonicas and melodicas, Bowed string instruments, Accordions/bayans/garmons, Folk and ethnic (Narodnye i etnicheskie) as its own top-level; amps sit under guitars

Woodbrass Paris: Guitars (instruments: electric, folk, classical, bass, ukuleles, traditional; amplification: guitar amps, bass amps, acoustic amps, effects pedals; accessories), Percussion, Keyboards, Studio, DJ, PA, Software, Gaming and streaming, Lighting, Winds, String Quartet, Cables, Accessories, Second Life (used); four physical stores split by guitar/e-drums, keys/studio, winds/sheet music, DJ/sound/light
Gear4music top navigation Guitars, Drums, Pianos, Orchestral, Studio, Live & PA; retailer of musical instruments from orchestral to rock with sites in UK, Germany, Spain, Sweden, Ireland

Vintage guitar valuation: same make/model/year/finish varies by originality and condition; player grade vs collector grade; vintage usually pre-1980; most valued pre-war Martin dreadnoughts and Gibson jumbos; value ladder driven by maker and model

Official Vintage Guitar Price Guide: sections electric guitars, acoustics, basses, amplifiers, effects, lap steels, steels, ukuleles, each ordered alphabetically by brand then by model with years of availability; values from 34 dealers; 42 Guitar Index

Amp types by technology (tube, solid-state, digital/modeling) and by form (head vs combo, cabinets, speakers, FRFR cabs); features such as effects loop, power scaling, line out, audio-interface function; buyers choose by where they play, wattage and style

Effects pedals divided into four functional categories (dynamic, time-based, frequency-based, modelling) then A to Z effect types (chorus, compressor, delay, distortion, fuzz, flanger, overdrive, phaser, reverb, tremolo, wah ...)

Guild of American Luthiers: nonprofit since 1972 for makers, repairers and restorers of stringed instruments; publishes instrument plans (for example 1935 Epiphone Olympic) and journal; shows the luthier as maker-craftsperson

Piano makers in five tiers: Concert Hall (Steinway, Bosendorfer, Fazioli), Professional Elite (Yamaha, Kawai, Bechstein), Serious Student and Home (Baldwin, Petrof, Grotrian), Value (Young Chang, Samick, Hailun), Budget; notes second lines of one maker (W. Hoffmann, Zimmermann by Bechstein) and that tier depends on the specific model and country of origin

Pianos in three tiers (luxury/bespoke, performance-grade, consumer-grade); Boston is designed by Steinway and built by Kawai, Essex is Steinway's entry-level line; warns of stencil brands; resale: Steinway, Yamaha, Kawai lead

Horniman Music Gallery: displays by keyboard instruments in the home, life-cycle use, makers and inventors (Boosey and Hawkes, Wheatstone concertina), and a classification display grouping instruments from around the world by how they produce sound; 9,500 instruments

Wagakki grouped as string (plucked: koto, biwa, shamisen; bowed: kokyu), wind (fue flutes, reed hichiriki, mouth organ sho) and percussion (drums such as kakko); a regional tradition is grouped by sound-source family
Wagakki Store (Umeya Gakki): Japanese traditional instruments sold as their own shop with Types and Maintain sections; shows traditional instruments as a separate retail field with own makers

Drum Center menu: Drum Sets (shell packs, with hardware, complete with cymbals, compact, used), Single Drums, Electronic Drums, Snare Drums, Cymbals (by maker: Zildjian, Paiste, Sabian, Istanbul Agop), Hand Drums (bongos, cajons, congas, djembes, doumbeks), World Percussion; Ludwig lines from entry to pro (Accent, Element Evolution, Classic Maple, Legacy Maple)

Drum kit maker tier ladders: Pearl Decade/Reference/Masters; TAMA Imperialstar/Superstar Classic/Starclassic/Star; Yamaha Stage Custom/Recording Custom/Tour Custom; Gretsch Catalina/Brooklyn/USA Custom; Sonor AQ2/SQ2/Delite; DW Design/Performance/Collector's; tiers entry-pro, mid-pro, premium, flagship, boutique are per maker line

Fender Japan 1982-2015 joint venture with Japanese distributors and FujiGen then Dyna Gakki as factories; country-of-origin labels (Made in Japan / Crafted in Japan) identify the factory; now Japan Exclusive series; shows brand, factory and country are separate facts
Japanese OEM factories (FujiGen, Dyna Gakki, Tokai, Terada, Matsumoku) that built guitars for Ibanez, Fender, Gibson, Greco, Yamaha etc.; a maker (factory) is distinct from the brand on the headstock
Non-exhaustive A to Z list of guitar brand-name companies including house brands; excludes most custom-only shops; separate list of luthiers for individual craftspeople

Specialist microphone retailer: Pro Audio > Microphones > Large Diaphragm; ranges from world-standard Neumann U87 to modern makers; shows named form (U87, U47 replica) as the unit buyers compare, with used and sold history

Thomann Guitars and Basses page: sub-categories E-Gitarren, Konzertgitarren, Westerngitarren, E-Baesse, Akustikbaesse, Ukulelen, Bluegrass, Travelgitarren, amps, strings, effects, pickups, parts; buyer text split acoustic vs electric and by beginner/advanced/pro; brand pages (Marcus Miller, Seymour Duncan) and manufacturer A to Z
Reverb Desktop Synths page: used, B-stock/mint and new listings by condition; listings are named products (for example Suzuki OM-84 Omnichord, Koma Elektronik FT201), showing model-level comparison
Reverb Price Guide values 240,000+ products by model and condition from sold listings; value attaches to model and condition, not to a generic kind
